subject: Fine tuning a multilevel poisson model

messages.author: 47e0d105424c0088
messages.subject: Fine tuning a multilevel poisson model
parts:
Folks,

I am trying to estimate a multilevel poisson regression with 
  • one first level predictor and its quadratic effect  (squared term)
  • and three second level group level predictors.
All  the second level predictors are standardized.

I have transformed the first level predictor and its squared term using the poly() function in R to get two orthogonal predictors.

My data consists of 7 count observations from each of 1000 subjects - a total of 7000 observations. 

The model runs but shows low n_eff sizes / rhat values with a default 4 chain run and thin=10. 

Not sure if more iterations will fix this or I need to improve the model code as below:

data {
    int<lower=0> N; // 7000 transactions
    int<lower=1> K; // 3 (including intercept)
    int<lower=1> J; // 1000
    int<lower=1> L; // 4 (including intercept)
    int<lower=1,upper=J> jj[N]; // group for individual
    matrix[N,K] x; // 7000 x 3
    matrix[J,L] u; // 1000 x 4
    int<lower=0> y[N];  //  7000 x 1 counts = 0,1,2,...
}

parameters {
    matrix[K,J] z;
    cholesky_factor_corr[K] L_Omega;
    vector<lower=0,upper=pi()/2>[K] tau_unif;
    matrix[L,K] gamma; // group coeffs
}

transformed parameters {
    matrix[J,K] beta;
    vector<lower=0>[K] tau; // prior scale
    for (k in 1:K) tau[k] = 2.5 * tan(tau_unif[k]);
    beta = u * gamma + (diag_pre_multiply(tau,L_Omega) * z)';
}

model {
    vector[N] log_lambda;

    // priors
    to_vector(z) ~ normal(0,1);
    tau ~ cauchy(0,2.5);
    L_Omega ~ lkj_corr_cholesky(2);
    to_vector(gamma) ~ normal(0,1);


    for (n in 1:N)
    log_lambda[n] = x[n] * beta[jj[n]]';


    y ~ poisson_log(log_lambda);

}

messages.author: 71c315ee557ff234
messages.subject: Re: Fine tuning a multilevel poisson model
parts: Dear Raghu,
for (k in 1:K) tau[k] = 2.5 * tan(tau_unif[k]);

tau ~ cauchy(0,2.5);

That would require a jacobian adjustment. Since tan is a non-linear transformation. 
What is the purpose of the above concept?

Andre

messages.author: fc5d3270037d7478
messages.subject: Re: Fine tuning a multilevel poisson model
parts:
Also, there shouldn't be a tau~cauchy(0, 2.5) if also using the transformation above it (which implies it). That's just a reparameterization of the Cauchy.

Jonah

messages.author: fc5d3270037d7478
messages.subject: Re: Fine tuning a multilevel poisson model
parts:
You shouldn't need a Jacobson adjustment if the prior is only placed on the primitive
parameter tau_raw or tau_unif or whatever it's called.

>
> My data consists of 7 count observations from each of 1000 subjects - a total of 7000 observations.
>
> The model runs but shows low n_eff sizes / rhat values with a default 4 chain run and thin=10.

Don't know why the model's mixing poorly, but I have a couple comments.

Thinning reduces n_eff, so you only want to thin if you run into memory
constraints saving draws.

>
> for (n in 1:N)
> log_lambda[n] = x[n] * beta[jj[n]]';

This can be simplified to:

log_lambda = rows_dot_product(x, beta[jj]);

but it's not going to be much if any faster.

- Bob
